core_principles: Altering the medial-lateral hand position (narrow, normal, or wide) changes shoulder muscle synergy and coordination during the push-up.

Two distinct muscle synergies control the push-up: Synergy 1 activates at the lowest position of the movement, while Synergy 2 is active before and after the lowest position (during the descent and ascent phases).
The most active muscles during these synergies correspond to shoulder and elbow extension and flexion.
specific_findings: The study analyzed 15 fitness athletes (weight: 68.35±7.18 kg, height: 175±3.40 cm, age: 24.50±7.5 years, and experience: 12±3 years).
Two synergies were extracted from the EMG of 14 upper body muscles using a Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) algorithm.
The minimum similarity of synergy coefficient was observed between normal and wide positions for both synergy 1 (SP=0.88) and synergy 2 (SP=0.79).
The minimum similarity of synergy weight was observed between normal and wide positions for both synergy 1 (SP=0.91) and synergy 2 (SP=0.84).

core_principles: Push-up variations (narrow, normal, and wide) recruit upper body muscles through distinct muscle synergies.
Synergy 1 is primarily activated at the lowest position of the push-up.
Synergy 2 is activated before and after reaching the lowest position of the push-up.
specific_findings: The local_VAF for all 14 muscles and push-up types (narrow, normal, wide) was greater than 0.75, demonstrating the reliability of the muscle synergies.
The minimum similarity of synergy coefficient was observed between normal and wide positions for both synergy 1 (SP=0.88) and synergy 2 (SP=0.79).
The minimum similarity of synergy weight was observed between normal and wide positions for both synergy 1 (SP=0.91) and synergy 2 (SP=0.84).

core_principles: The standard push-up involves two distinct muscle synergies extracted from 14 muscles.
Synergy 1 is activated at the lowest position of the push-up, corresponding to the transition phase.
Synergy 2 is active before and after the lowest position, corresponding to the descent and ascent phases.
Varying hand positions (narrow, normal, and wide) alters how the central nervous system coordinates and controls muscle groups.
The greatest difference in muscle coordination strategies (CNS control) occurs between the normal and wide hand positions.
specific_findings: Two synergies were extracted from the EMG of 14 muscles.

The minimum similarity of both synergy coefficient and synergy weight were observed between normal and wide positions (Synergy 1 coefficient similarity of 0.88 and Synergy 2 coefficient similarity of 0.79).
Synergy 1 similarity coefficients across hand positions were: Narrow VS Normal = 0.91, Normal VS Wide = 0.88, and Narrow VS Wide = 0.96.
Synergy 2 similarity coefficients across hand positions were: Narrow VS Normal = 0.85, Normal VS Wide = 0.79, and Narrow VS Wide = 0.95.
Synergy Weight Synergy 1 similarity values were: Narrow VS Normal = 0.94, Normal VS Wide = 0.91, and Narrow VS Wide = 0.92.
Synergy Weight Synergy 2 similarity values were: Narrow VS Normal = 0.86, Normal VS Wide = 0.84, and Narrow VS Wide = 0.89.
